pending.h: Hearn Accuses Dana White Of Mocking British Fans Over Fury-Joshua
pending.sum: Hearn claims Dana White barely promoted Fury-Joshua in America and doesn't want it to succeed because it's staying in the UK.
pending.q: I think Dana White's taking the piss out of the British fans.
pending.ctx: Interview with iFL TV, two weeks before Fury vs Joshua
body: Eddie Hearn went after Dana White in an interview with iFL TV. He said White and Nick Khan are advising on the Fury-Joshua event and that the undercard shows what they are doing. In his words: “They don't know what they're doing.”

Hearn pointed to the late ring time, which he says is aimed at American viewers. He asked who has been promoting the fight in America and said the answer was Dana White, with what he called one post. He claimed they don't want it to succeed because they are annoyed it is still in the UK.

Hearn said he is not involved in promoting the fight, though he has a fighter on the card. He said that if he were running it, the buildup would have been far bigger. “No one drives content like us.” He also said he believes Netflix will overturn the undercard order and move Cordina vs Lara onto the main card.
Why it matters: Fury vs Joshua is two weeks away, and the biggest promoter in British boxing is publicly accusing the UFC boss of undermining the build. That adds a promotional feud to fight week.

pending.h: Sauerland Offers Hearn And White 10 Million Each To Fight
pending.sum: Promoter Kalle Sauerland says he has agreed terms with Eddie Hearn, while Dana White would only do it in a gym. He wants charity money added.
pending.q: So my solution would be you know we'll do it in a gym.
body: Kalle Sauerland confirmed he has put 10 million each on the table for Eddie Hearn and Dana White to settle their beef in the ring. The host noted that Hearn had said he is worth more than that. Sauerland brushed it off as Hearn talking.

Sauerland says terms are already agreed with Hearn. He also says he heard White say in an interview that he would like to do it, but in a gym. Sauerland's answer is a gym fight sold on pay-per-view, with money added for charity. He also said a private jet has been thrown in so travel is covered.

The host pointed out that Hearn has not confirmed he would do it for charity. Sauerland said he is sure Hearn does a lot for charity and promised to put his own company's profit into it too. He said it would be “we'll add money to charity on it as well.” He pitched it as short rounds rather than a 12-round fight.

Why it matters: The Hearn and White feud has been running for weeks. This is the first concrete offer to settle it, though only Sauerland says Hearn has agreed, and White's gym-only stance is a long way from a signed deal.

pending.h: Hysa Weighs In 15 Pounds Heavier Than Kabayel For WBC Showdown
pending.sum: Both heavyweights have stepped on the scale and faced off for the final time before tomorrow's 12-round WBC title fight in Kabayel's first defense.
body: Challenger Nelson Hysa weighed in at 113.2 kg (249.5 lb). Defending WBC heavyweight champion Agit Kabayel came in at 106.4 kg (234.5 lb), so Hysa carries 15 lb more into the ring.

The announcer introduced both men as undefeated. Hysa has 25 wins, 23 by knockout, and holds the WBO global title. Kabayel has 27 wins, 19 by knockout, and is making the first defense of his world title.
The two fighters then faced off for the final time. The fight is scheduled for 12 rounds tomorrow, live worldwide on DAZN, and is promoted by Frank Warren's Queensberry with Gold Star Promotions.
Why it matters: Both men have now weighed in and the face-off is done, so the unbeaten champion and the heavy-handed challenger meet for the WBC title tomorrow, with Hysa the bigger man.

pending.h: Hearn Urges Fans To Push Cordina Onto Fury-Joshua Main Card
pending.sum: Hearn says he was baffled Cordina vs Lara wasn't on the main card and believes fan pressure will force Netflix to move it up.
pending.q: And I believe Netflix will have no choice but to elevate Joe Cordina to the main card.
pending.ctx: Matchroom Boxing video message to fans
body: Eddie Hearn says he was "completely baffled" to learn that Joe Cordina's fight with Mauricio Lara was not on the main portion of the Fury vs Joshua card. He called the matchup a brilliant fight and said giving it main card billing is simple common sense.
Hearn gave two reasons Cordina is on the card at all. One is his own pushing and refusal to give up. The other is “because of the public response and support.”

He is now asking fans to keep the pressure on, repeating what he said on his story: “do your thing, guys.” Hearn says he believes Netflix will have no choice but to move Cordina up, and that they will.
Why it matters: Fans who want Cordina vs Lara on the main card are being told their noise could change the running order. Nothing has been confirmed, and for now Hearn is making a public case.

pending.h: Pettis Says Doubters Will Be Shocked By His Wrestling Debut
pending.sum: Anthony Pettis says no one has seen his wrestling and expects to surprise the people counting him out against Arman Tsarukyan at RAF 15.
pending.q: Might as well go against the champ. If I'm going to go try this for my first time, might as well be against the best right now.
pending.ctx: Interview with MMA Fighting ahead of RAF 15
body: Anthony Pettis says he loved the switch-up that put him in a wrestling match with Arman Tsarukyan at RAF 15. He called himself a fan of Tsarukyan and praised the way he is performing in MMA and in wrestling.

Pettis said this is his first wrestling match. He wanted to get his feet wet, but when the Tsarukyan opportunity came up he decided that if he was going to try it, he might as well face the best right now.

Asked about people who think Tsarukyan will go in and run him over, Pettis told them to watch on Saturday. He said “no one's seen my wrestling” and that he has never had to do straight wrestling before. He expects people to be shocked.
Why it matters: Pettis is a big underdog by his own admission, and he is betting that a style nobody has seen from him can upset one of the sport's most in-form wrestlers.

pending.h: Fury Cleared By Boxing Board For Joshua Fight, Davies Says
pending.sum: Journalist Gareth A. Davies says the board cleared Fury's medicals after mental health headlines, so the December 11 fight against Joshua is on.
pending.q: there is not an issue around his mental health right now in order for him to progress and fight Anthony Joshua on December the 11th
body: Davies says he spoke to the boxing board and was told Fury cleared his medicals on Thursday night. He says the promoter was informed on Friday morning.

The questions came after a Netflix documentary and its press release, which carried comments from Paris Fury about his mental health. Davies says the release quoted her describing mild schizophrenia, but that Fury was never diagnosed with it. He says Fury has had bouts of mania linked to bipolar disorder. He says the Fury camp asked Netflix to remove the scene.

Davies argues the story was blown out of proportion. He says the board was simply responding to the noise, and that the retrospective comments needed investigating. In his words, “this fight was never under threat” unless one of the fighters was unwell.

Why it matters: The clearance removes doubt over the biggest British heavyweight fight in years, two weeks before the bell. Fury is cleared to face Joshua in Cardiff, and the Joshua camp has stayed quiet on the matter.

pending.h: Odiase Says Joshua Needs Legendary Goat Energy To Beat Fury
pending.sum: Heavyweight Emanuel Odiase says Joshua must bring the right mindset against Fury, and calls the fight huge despite both being past their primes.
pending.q: That legendary goat energy, bro. Then he can beat anyone.
pending.ctx: Interview with Seconds Out ahead of his fight with Mike Perez
body: Heavyweight Emanuel Odiase, who says he fights Mike Perez tomorrow, was asked whether Anthony Joshua has to be like Muhammad Ali to beat Tyson Fury. His answer was about mindset. Joshua needs the right energy, and with it Odiase believes he can beat anyone.

He then dropped the jokes and said Joshua has to arrive in the right frame of mind. “AJ's got to come with the right energy.” Odiase added that he thinks Joshua is doing exactly that, and hopes both men come in at their best.
Earlier in the interview, Odiase said Fury and Joshua waited a long time to fight. In his view, both are past their primes. He still believes the fight is a big one.
Why it matters: Fury and Joshua meet on December 11, and a rising heavyweight is telling fans the outcome could come down to Joshua's mindset rather than just skills.

pending.h: Kraus Says Whitaker Isn't Ready And Vows To Knock Him Out
pending.sum: Gradus Kraus says he would stop Ben Whitaker if they met, picks Bivol to beat Callum Smith, and wants a world title shot next year.
pending.q: for 12 rounds I think Whitaker is not ready yet and for sure not when he is with me in the ring.
pending.ctx: Interview with Seconds Out, the day before his fight
body: Gradus Kraus was asked if he would fight Ben Whitaker next. He said yes and promised a stoppage: “I will knock him out”. He says his pressure and power are better than what Whitaker faced in his last fight, and that Whitaker doesn't like pressure.
Kraus gave Whitaker credit for his early work. He called him fast, with good distance, and sharp. But he pointed to the closing rounds of Whitaker's last fight and said it is over when it is over.

Kraus also said he is ready for his fight tomorrow night against Adam Deans and that Deans is going to feel “real power”. He wants a world title fight, hopes it comes next year, and says he would stop both Willie Hutchinson and Joshua Buatsi in one night. On Bivol, he picks him to beat Callum Smith but says he would pressure Bivol and land his heavy punches.
Why it matters: Kraus is calling out Whitaker and a world title shot in the same interview. A win tomorrow night would give those calls more weight.

pending.h: Brown Open To Moving Cordina Higher On Fury-Joshua Undercard
pending.sum: After Eddie Hearn's gripe over Joe Cordina's slot, Spencer Brown says the Welshman's placement may change. He also defends the undercard as Netflix-driven.
pending.q: I think Joe deserves to be right at the top of the card
body: Spencer Brown says Joe Cordina's spot on the Fury vs Joshua undercard could be changed. Asked about Eddie Hearn's complaint over where Cordina sits, Brown said it is something they will look at to see if they can move him up the card.
Brown said Cordina is a local Cardiff lad whom everybody was crying out for, and gave Hearn credit for getting him on the show. He also argued Cordina belongs at the top of the undercard.

He defended the undercard overall, pointing to Netflix's global audience and the need for international fighters. On who controls the card, he was blunt: “They're paying for it.” He said they will push to get Cordina further up but can only do what they can.
Why it matters: British fans have grumbled about the undercard, and Cordina's placement is the clearest flashpoint. Nothing is confirmed, but Brown has left the door open to a change.

pending.h: Shalom Vows To Enforce Contract Over Bakole's Wilder Fight
pending.sum: Ben Shalom calls the Bakole situation a mess and says he will enforce his contractual rights, with a week or two of drama ahead.
pending.q: Look, we will uh we will enforce our contractual rights and that's it.
pending.ctx: Interview with Seconds Out in Amsterdam
body: Promoter Ben Shalom says he will go by the letter of the contract with Martin Bakole. Bakole has been announced as the replacement opponent for Opetaia to face Deontay Wilder.

Shalom says he doesn't know why whoever advises the fighter doesn't just say to “sort out sort out the mess first”. He says his side are reasonable people and things can be sorted. But he can't tell his staff, lawyers and finance people not to enforce a contract, and says the situation has put them in a position where they have to. He called it a shame for the fighter, adding “it always ends in tears”.

He also aimed at Zuffa. He said he couldn't believe a British fighter wasn't offered the chance, and that Zuffa's fingerprints were all over the undercard. He said the whole thing is a mess and that it comes down to Zuffa. He expects a very interesting week or two.
Why it matters: if Shalom follows through, Bakole's place opposite Wilder on the Fury-Joshua bill could be in doubt just as the card is being finalised.

pending.h: Atlas Says Hysa Won't Last The Night Against Kabayel
pending.sum: Teddy Atlas sees Hysa's right hand as his only real chance and expects Kabayel's pressure to end it early in Germany.
pending.q: he is going from the waiting pool to the ocean. And he'll probably get drowned.
pending.ctx: Fight preview on THE FIGHT with Teddy Atlas
body: Teddy Atlas previewed WBC heavyweight champion Agit Kabayel's defense against Nelson Hysa in Germany and picked the champion to stop him. The show described Hysa as 25-0 with 23 knockouts and 42 years old. It said he turned pro at 37 and is an 18-1 underdog.

Atlas says Hysa's one path to an upset is the right hand. He admits he doesn't know how much power it carries, because the opponents it has knocked out have not been high level. In his words, “I just don't know how hard he punches with the right hand.” He argues the jump in competition will be too big for the Albanian.

On Kabayel, Atlas praises a relentless, thick-boned pressure fighter with a good chin and a strong body attack, and he compares him to Daniel Dubois. He does see a flaw. Kabayel can get anxious for the knockout and take extra shots, especially uppercuts, and a straight right can catch him if he jabs from too close.
Atlas says he doesn't see Hysa lasting the whole night. He is leaning toward a no on the fight going the distance once the props are posted. His official pick is reserved for his subscription site.

Why it matters: A respected voice expects an early finish for the champion, while Hysa's backers are hoping for an upset. Atlas's one caveat is that nobody knows how hard Hysa's right hand really lands against a heavyweight of this level.

pending.h: Hearn Says Fury And Joshua Will Punch For Ringwalk Order
pending.sum: Eddie Hearn says a signed contract addendum has Fury and Joshua hitting a punch machine in fight week, with the top score walking second.
pending.q: there will be a punch machine on fight week that both fighters will punch and the biggest score, the highest score will walk second.
pending.ctx: Interview clip released by Matchroom Boxing
body: Eddie Hearn says the order of the Fury vs Joshua ringwalks will be settled by a contest. A punch machine will be set up in fight week, and both fighters will take a shot at it.
The fighter who posts the highest score will walk second. Hearn says the arrangement is part of the most recent contract, in an addendum. He says Netflix apparently likes the idea too.
Hearn stressed it is official, calling it “signed and papered.” He also appeared to suggest Tyson Fury may not want to play along, but said “it's in our contract.”
Why it matters: ringwalk order is usually a status issue between two big names, and here it comes down to a contractual punching contest in fight week, ahead of the December 11 fight.

pending.h: Spencer Brown Says Fury Fight Is On Despite Health Claims
pending.sum: Spencer Brown says there is no diagnosis behind the schizophrenia reports, that Fury is in great spirits, and that the Joshua fight is happening.
pending.q: there's no way in the world that Tyson Fury was schizophrenic
body: Spencer Brown shot down recent reports about Tyson Fury's mental health. He said there is no diagnosis, that the issue is historical, and that it resurfaced because of a comment in a documentary segment that he says was never due to air.

Brown called the coverage sensationalism and said Fury has been open about his mental health struggles and should be praised for it, not criticised. He said the boxing board has cleared Fury to fight and that there was never any doubt about it.

He also said Anthony Joshua's side got in touch to ask if Fury was all right and if the fight was still on. Brown's answer: “The fight's on.” He said he speaks to Fury every day, that Fury is in the best headspace he has seen him in, and that he arrives in England next week.
Why it matters: With the fight two weeks away, the headlines had raised questions about whether it would go ahead. Brown's camp is now saying it will, and that Fury is fit to fight.

pending.h: Napper Says Eubank Jr vs Brook Decision Due In Days
pending.sum: Eubank Jr's manager says a decision on a Kell Brook fight is coming within days. He also gave the likely weight, location and timing.
pending.q: It's closer than it's ever been ever before.
pending.who: Napper, manager of Chris Eubank Jr
pending.ctx: Interview with Boxing King Media in Dubai
body: Napper says talks for Chris Eubank Jr vs Kell Brook are further along than at any earlier point. He says the camp is “more hot than cold”. A decision on whether the fight happens should come in the next couple of days, though he wouldn't say when an announcement might follow.

He says the team is trying to get a few things over the line. If they do, there's a fight. If they don't, there isn't. He wouldn't say who would promote it, noting that Eubank Jr is a free agent who can work with whoever offers the most.

On the details, Napper says it would be at super middleweight with no weight clauses on either fighter. The location would probably be the UK, and the timing is “First quarter of next year.” He says Eubank Jr has long been up for the fight and has wanted it since Brook beat Khan.

Why it matters: A Eubank Jr vs Brook fight would be a big domestic night in the UK, and Napper says any other names linked to Eubank Jr, including Conor Benn, are off the table until this one is settled.

pending.h: Kape Tells Van His Title Reign Ends In Toronto
pending.sum: Manel Kape says he's on another level from champion Joshua Van and predicts a body-head attack that ends with Van dropped in Toronto.
pending.q: You cannot compare me and him. This is this is a big insult.
body: Manel Kape says flyweight champion Joshua Van's time is up. Speaking to MMA Fighting before their UFC 336 fight in Toronto, Kape said he has no hard feelings and isn't underestimating Van. But he called this "the end of the road" and said the belt is going home with him.

Kape said he was more impressed by how Pantoja fought than by Van's performance. He said Pantoja was emotional in that fight and paid the price. He gave Van credit for maturity on the ground, but he dismissed his striking as that of a regular fighter and said they are in different levels.

He was blunt about the gap. Kape said “whatever Joshua Van do, I do I do 10 times better.” As for how it ends, he predicts a body-head attack that wears Van down, followed by a finish. In his words, he'll “drop him like I drop everyone.”
Why it matters: Kape has waited a long time for this title shot and is selling it as a changing of the guard. His confidence adds some edge to a flyweight title fight that is usually respectful.
